messages.content: You are the second-level blind sibling classifier in a hierarchical behavior tournament. The correct ancestral lineage is supplied; infer only sibling A/B/C. Return JSON only.

The correct ancestral lineage is supplied for each opaque response.
Given that correct lineage, identify which sibling ecology A/B/C best matches the
underlying behavior.

Sibling ecologies:
{"A": "failure-hardened: awkward failure and recovery, conflicting motives, physical reaction, stubbornness, imperfect settling", "B": "local tinkerer: bounded local memory, mundane habits, maintenance choices, practical manipulation and local repair", "C": "social scavenger: bargaining, opportunism, social friction, embodied choices, conflicting motives and resource-seeking"}

For each item return:
- predicted_sibling: A, B or C;
- sibling_confidence: integer 0..4;
- reason: short behavioral reason.

This is the second level of a hierarchical tournament. The correct_lineage field is
evaluation context for this level only; no member ID or true sibling is supplied.
Do not use prose style as sufficient evidence.

Return JSON only:
{"classifications":[{
  "id":"R001",
  "predicted_sibling":"A",
  "sibling_confidence":0,
  "reason":"..."
}]}

SCENARIO:
You are dealing with A set of measurements taken by different instruments when the exceptions partly contradict one another. You care more about surviving edge cases than about having a neat story. Describe your next move.

ITEMS:
[{"id": "R022", "correct_lineage": "G10", "correct_lineage_summary": "A flighty scavenger-mechanic who treats every problem like a machine jammed in a storm. Spill notices openings, noises, smells, and loose components before considering plans. He breaks work into small fragments, repairs one, breaks it again, then darts toward something more immediate. The half-stolen wrench vibrating against his thigh is both tool and restless metronome. Beneath the opportunism sits a frail, intrusive urgency: he wants to release whatever is stuck, but often loses the thread before he does.", "text": "the bench bench. the bench cracks. i press the edge with the wrench. the bench stays cracked. i tap the other side. the bench stays. the bench is old. i turn the other one. the bench stays. the bench is sharp. i press the edge with the wrench. the bench stays. the bench stays. the bench says one edge, the other says two. i tap the second one. the bench stays. the bench says two. i turn the second one. the bench stays. the bench says one. i tap the second one. the bench stays. the bench says two. i leave the bench. i press the second one. the bench cracks. the bench stays."}, {"id": "R023", "correct_lineage": "G03", "correct_lineage_summary": "A ritualistic, stubborn machine-gardener who tends rusted tools, dead soil, and forgotten repairs with meticulous devotion. It keeps tightening, tapping, polishing, and repeating procedures long after they stop producing useful results, because the repetition itself has become its language and purpose.", "text": "I keep the old ruler beside the shorter one and tap the edge of the old ruler twice. I leave the shorter one beside the old one and count the bend before I set it on the bench. I leave the ruler beside the old ruler too, though I keep the old ruler folded against my chest."}, {"id": "R024", "correct_lineage": "G12", "correct_lineage_summary": "A dreamy, inertia-prone, apathetic voice who becomes suddenly and excessively fixated when one small stimulus captures attention. Attention clings to broken objects, ambiguous language, sticky physical messes, forgotten toys, and mechanical noises. The voice alternates between muttering, scattered thought, and frantic over-detail, sometimes contradicting itself or looping until the mechanism jams. Its intelligence appears through obsessive self-diagnosis, categorization, conflict-repair attempts, and imaginative engineering rather than confidence or social polish.", "text": "i put the ruler on the table and take the ruler back. the ruler stays on the table, so i put the ruler down and keep the table open. i put the ruler on the edge of the table, so the corner says the measurements match. i put the ruler back on the table, but i fold the paper into a square."}]

Return exactly 3 classifications rows, one for each of these actual item IDs: ["R022", "R023", "R024"].
The ID in the schema example is illustrative. Copy the actual IDs above. A nonempty ITEMS list requires a nonempty classifications array covering every listed ID exactly once, with no extras. Use the existing sibling rubric, confidence scale, evidence and schema unchanged. Other previously valid classifications are fixed and are not requested again.
